chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Nadr ibn Suweyd, from Yahya ibn Imran ibn Ali Al-Halby, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the Azan before Fajr, so he said: 'If it is in a congregation, then no (it is not done), and if he is alone, then there is no problem (it is permissible).'
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to call the Azan before Fajr prayer when alone versus in a congregation?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the permissibility of the pre-Fajr Azan by distinguishing between congregational and solitary contexts, reflecting the scholarly view that the Azan serves primarily to announce the prayer time to the community. In a group setting, the established practice is to avoid it to prevent confusion or redundancy, whereas an individual is permitted to recite it to remind themselves and any nearby listeners. This ruling underscores the practical function of the Azan as a public notification rather than a rigid ritual obligation in all circumstances.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Al Nazar Bin Suweyd, from Yahya Bin Imran Bin Ali Al Halby who said,
‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about the Azān before Al-Fajr, so heasws said: ‘When it was in a Jam’at, so no, and when he was alone, so there is no problem’.
en.sarwar: 23. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Yahya ibn ‘Imran ibn Ali al-Halabiy who has said the following: “
I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about Adhan before dawn. He (the Imam) said, ‘If it is for congregation, it is not acceptable, but if one is alone, then it is not harmful.’”
